content.user_title: Search the Web Semantically with Exa
content.value_statement: Keyword searches can miss conceptually relevant sources and related content. This skill guides Exa API searches for semantic discovery, category filtering, and structured research.
actual_capabilities: Guides semantic searches through the Exa API.
Supports finding content related to a known source or topic.
Frames category-focused searches for companies, people, and research papers.
Structures multi-step research requests around a clear topic.
Directs users to configure the Exa API key through environment variables.
limitations: Requires an Exa API key and access to the Exa service.
Does not include executable integration code in the reviewed SKILL.md file.
Search quality depends on Exa coverage, query clarity, and selected categories.
Results require source verification before decisions or publication.

use_cases.title: Map a Market
use_cases.description: Find conceptually related companies and organize results for comparison.

use_cases.title: Discover Research
use_cases.description: Search for papers by topic and discover related material beyond exact keyword matches.

use_cases.title: Scout Related Content
use_cases.description: Locate similar articles and sources for planning, differentiation, and fact checking.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Semantic Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Exa to search for sources about [topic]. Return relevant results with titles, links, and one-sentence relevance notes.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs conceptually relevant sources for one topic.

prompt_templates.title: Search a Specific Category
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Exa for [company, person, or research paper] results about [topic]. Apply the closest category and explain why each result fits.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user wants results limited to a defined entity type.

prompt_templates.title: Find Similar Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [source or topic], find semantically similar content with Exa. Group results by similarity and note meaningful differences.
prompt_templates.scenario: A researcher wants alternatives or related sources.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Structured Research Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [research question] with Exa across [categories]. Use several semantic queries, compare recurring evidence, identify disagreements, and present a source-linked synthesis.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs a multi-query research synthesis.

output_examples.input: Find research papers about evaluating retrieval-augmented generation.
output_examples.output: A ranked paper list with titles, source links, and concise relevance notes. Related papers are grouped by evaluation method.

output_examples.input: Find articles similar to this source and explain the differences.
output_examples.output: Groups of semantically similar articles, each with a source link, similarity note, and clear statement of important differences.

best_practices: State the research question, desired categories, and date range before searching.
Use environment variables for the Exa API key and never place secrets in prompts.
Verify important claims against primary sources before publishing or making decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague topics when a precise concept or category is available.
Do not treat semantic similarity as proof that sources support the same conclusion.
Do not expose API keys, private documents, or confidential query details.

faq.question: What is required to use this skill?
faq.answer: An Exa API key and access to a compatible Exa integration are required.

faq.question: Does this skill support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How does semantic search differ from keyword search?
faq.answer: Semantic search targets conceptual relevance, while keyword search mainly matches terms. Results still depend on query quality and Exa coverage.

faq.question: Can this skill find similar content?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a known source or clear topic and request semantically related results.

faq.question: Which search categories are documented?
faq.answer: The reviewed skill lists companies, people, and research papers as examples. Other categories depend on Exa support.

faq.question: Does this skill verify every result?
faq.answer: No. Review source quality, publication dates, and primary evidence before relying on results.
